endpoints.notes: Official endpoint, best of the four. Chain 0xa4b1. 40 serial calls = 5.3 req/s with 0x429 across ~250 requests (did not stress concurrency). eth_getLogs: NO hard block-range cap and NO silent truncation (address-filtered Initialize over 1,000,000 blocks returned 527, identical to 10x100k splits); but high-cardinality queries time out with -32000 'log query timed out' (PoolManager Swap over 200k blocks failed; 50k = 6683 results OK). Batch of 50 returned 50/50, ids preserved. Practice: chunk address-filtered getLogs at ~250k blocks, keep Swap/high-fanout chunks <=50k, 50-item batches, >=0.2s gap.

Alias arbitrum-one.publicnode.com behaves the same. chainId/blockNumber/batch(50) OK. ARCHIVE getLogs on historical ranges returns HTTP 403 -32602 'Archive requests require a personal token'; range cap -32701 'exceed maximum block range: 10000'. Usable only for head/recent state, not a 7-day log census.
chainId/block OK. getLogs code 35 'ranges over 10000 blocks are not supported on free plan'. Batch >3 rejected code 31. Fallback only.
CONNECT tunnel failed, response 502 (unreachable via egress proxy / endpoint down). Not usable.
No response within 15s timeout (curl 28). Not usable.
-32000 'Unauthorized: You must authenticate your request with an API key'. Requires a key, not a public endpoint.

feed: wss://arb1-feed.arbitrum.io/feed WORKS. WebSocket handshake succeeded in 0.45s; read one frame = 636 bytes of JSON {version, messages}; compression=deflate. Each frame message is a Nitro broadcast: m.sequenceNumber (e.g. 491697733), m.message.message.header.kind == 3 (batch), header.timestamp present, and inner.l2Msg is base64 - exactly the protocol src/flip_engine.py feed_loop / decode_batch expects (kind 3 batches of 8-byte-length segments, kind 4 single tx). This is the same first-come sequencer-ordering feed the engine fronts on; it is live and decodable with the existing reader (set FEED_URL to this, FEED_COMPRESSION=deflate). Note: the sequence number is the feed's own counter, not the L2 block number.
limits: arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc is the only endpoint fit for a census: >=5 req/s serial with no 429 seen, 50-item batches, address-filtered eth_getLogs over very large ranges with no silent truncation (chunk at ~250k blocks; keep high-cardinality Swap chunks <=50k or you hit 'log query timed out'). publicnode is head/recent + batch only (historical getLogs needs a token, 10k-block cap). drpc is a thin fallback (10k-block getLogs, batch<=3). llamarpc/1rpc/ankr unusable (502 / timeout / key required).
